fields.description: The deployment this person is assigned to. Set once: moving somebody between deployments would rewrite what they agreed to, so the honest way to do it is to withdraw this assignment and raise another.
fields.label: Deployment

fields.description: Who is assigned. Set once, for the same reason the deployment is: an assignment is one person's record of being asked and answering, and pointing it at somebody else would silently transfer their answer.
fields.label: Volunteer

fields.description: The exact terms this person was asked to accept, copied from the deployment when the assignment is raised and never followed live. This is the whole reason VMMS Terms of Reference is submittable: accepting an assignment is accepting these terms, so the assignment records which document that was. An amendment to the terms afterwards produces a new document and leaves this one pointing where it always pointed.
fields.label: Terms of Reference

fields.description: Where the work happens, copied from the deployment. Held on the assignment rather than read through the link because core filters each doctype on a field of its own: an assignment scoped through its deployment would be an assignment nobody could scope.
fields.label: Geo Node

fields.description: Where this assignment stands. Assigned: a coordinator placed this person, and no question was asked. Pending: they were asked and have not answered. Accepted and Declined are their answer. Withdrawn is the coordinator taking the assignment back. Assigned and Accepted are the two that count as being on the deployment — they fill a place against the headcount and they are what lets time be logged against the deployment. Every move goes through deployment/services/assignment.py::assert_transition, which holds the whole grammar; nothing sets this field directly.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: What this person does on the deployment. leader: the one who leads it in the field, and whom updates and reports are addressed to. member: everybody else. Held here rather than on the deployment so that leadership is a fact about somebody's participation and shows up in their own history; a deployment admits at most one leader, which assignment.py checks across the whole deployment rather than on this row alone.
fields.label: Role

fields.description: When this person's own deployment begins, copied from the deployment and editable afterwards. Somebody joining a fortnight-long response for its last three days is ordinary, and a single pair of dates on the deployment could not say so.
fields.label: Starts

fields.description: When this person's own deployment ends. Refused if it falls before their start date.
fields.label: Ends

fields.description: When they were asked. Blank on an assignment a coordinator placed directly, which is a different fact from having been asked and stayed silent.
fields.label: Asked On

fields.description: When they answered. Written by the service alongside the status, never on its own, so a record cannot say it was answered on a date and not say what the answer was.
fields.label: Answered On

fields.description: What the volunteer said when they answered — why they cannot go, what they would need, when they could. In their own words, and the one field on this record they write.
fields.label: Their Note

fields.description: The day they actually joined. Distinct from the start date, which is the plan: somebody who arrived two days late joined two days late, and a deployment report that could not say so would be wrong.
fields.label: Joined On

fields.description: The day they left, where that is earlier than the end. Leaving is recorded, never removed: withdrawing the assignment instead would make the time they actually served unfilable, which is precisely backwards.
fields.label: Left On

fields.description: Anything about how this person's deployment went. Never read by code.
fields.label: Participation Notes

fields.description: The coordinator's own note on this assignment — why this person, what they are bringing, what was agreed on the phone. Copied from the deployment's note when the assignment is raised in bulk, and editable afterwards.
fields.label: Notes
